findings.summary: The caption prints one field under one label, 'Qualified saddle gap', in both figures, but that field names different pairs of nulls in each. For frame 137 the 12.15 cm is the lower solved-saddle to EFIT gap; for frame 146 the 221.85 cm is, by the reviewed run's own receipt, the upper selected qualified saddle to lower EFIT reference, while the continued lower gap is 13.90 cm -- sixteen times smaller and the number a reader of this non-converged arm most needs. Nothing in the rendered picture names either endpoint, so a reader takes 221.85 cm as the solved-versus-EFIT X-point mismatch the zoom is there to show. The caption should name the two nulls it spans, and the lower continued gap belongs beside it. Anchor: scripts/prototypes/diiid_warmup_admission/render.py:235, f"Qualified saddle gap {100 * record['x_point_distance_m']:.2f} cm".

disposition.reason: Read-only review; the window is computed in the render script and the correction is a follow-on change to it.

findings.summary: Both figures draw their X-point inset over a fixed 0.5 m window (xlim and ylim at feature +- 0.25 m), and the caption beneath each reports a distance that window is supposed to support. For frame 137 the reported 12.15 cm is 24 % of the window width and the inset shows it. For frame 146 the reported 2.2185 m is 4.4 times the window width, so the two endpoints the caption measures cannot both appear in the inset at all: the zoom shows a local tangle of solved contours whose relation to the printed 221.85 cm cannot be read off the picture. Either the inset should be sized from the distance it illustrates, or the caption should say the zoom is a local view and the gap is read from the main panel. Anchor: scripts/prototypes/diiid_warmup_admission/render.py:199-200.

disposition.reason: Read-only review; the marker vocabulary lives in the render script and in nova.media.poloidal, so changing it is a follow-on node.

findings.summary: The legend distinguishes 'solved saddles' from 'EFIT X-point' by hue alone: both entries are the same open 'X' marker with mfc='none', drawn #2E8B57 against #7F7F7F (render.py:251-254 and :260). The axis pair does not have this problem, because the solved axis is filled and the EFIT axis is hollow. In the dense lower region of both figures a reader hunting the admitted EFIT X-point has only a green-versus-grey judgement to separate two markers that denote different physical objects, and the same weakness applies in a greyscale reproduction of the evidence page. A distinct marker shape for one of the two would remove the reliance on hue.

findings.summary: Neither rendered figure carries a title, and the caption lines beneath each panel name only 'support', 'residual' and 'Qualified saddle gap'. The frame number and the machine appear nowhere in the image, so a PNG lifted out of the evidence fragment -- in a slide, a thumbnail, or the powers-of-ten listing -- cannot be told from the other one except by reading its file name. Identity lives in the file name and should also stand in the caption; a single line naming the machine and frame would make the picture self-describing. Anchor: scripts/prototypes/diiid_warmup_admission/render.py:203, which writes only the arm word ('before'/'after').
